study.title: GABRB3 Gene Polymorphisms Influences the Analgesic Response to Acupuncture Treatment in Patients With Chronic Knee Pain: A Randomized Controlled Neuroimaging Transcriptomics Study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled neuroimaging transcriptomics study; five-arm parallel-group RCT with 2-week run-in period and 2-week intervention period; centralized randomization, 1:1:1:1:1 ratio
study.randomization: Centralized randomization using SAS 9.2 software; allocation sequence generated by independent central randomization center; allocation concealment via sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes; executed sequentially by telephone randomization administrator
study.blinding: Participant-investigator double-blinding for SC/PB group; single-blinding for VA/SA group; triple assurance via standardized participant operational procedures, independent evaluators for data collection, and third-party statistical analysis
study.population: Patients with chronic knee pain due to knee osteoarthritis (KOA); aged 40–60 years; right-handed; non-kinship Han Chinese with long-term residence (>10 years) in Chengdu city
study.disease_condition: Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) with chronic knee pain
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) meeting the diagnostic criteria for KOA (ACR 1991 revised criteria); (2) aged 40–60 years; (3) right-handed; (4) persistent knee pain for the past 3 months, with an average VAS pain score of ≥3 points recorded within 2 weeks prior to enrollment; (5) a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 0-II, confirmed by X-ray examination; (6) no history of relevant therapy, including the use of KOA-related therapeutic drugs within 2 weeks prior to enrollment, acupuncture received within the past 1 month, or intra-articular sodium hyaluronate injection within the past 6 months; (6) signed informed consent obtained from the patient or their legal representatives
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) any history of severe somatic diseases (e.g., major primary neurological or cardiovascular diseases), rheumatoid arthritis, or other chronic pain conditions (including craniocerebral trauma accompanied by impaired consciousness); (2) history of substance abuse (e.g., alcohol or drug abuse) or psychiatric disorders; (3) contraindications to MRI scan or acupuncture, or celecoxib allergy; (4) pregnancy or lactation; (5) current participation in any other clinical trials

arms.dropouts: 8 patients eliminated: 4 with time restriction, 3 head movement, 1 accidental injury
10 patients eliminated: 1 with time restriction, 3 head movement, 6 no genetic data
8 patients eliminated: 4 with personal reason, 2 head movement, 1 intolerable to celecoxib, 1 no genetic data
7 patients eliminated: 3 with personal reason, 3 head movement, 1 no genetic data
9 patients eliminated: 3 with personal reason, 1 head movement, 3 no genetic data, 2 received treatment
Combined post-hoc group: VA (n=28) + SA (n=26) pooled due to no significant difference in primary outcomes between VA and SA

extraction_notes.note: Multiple referenced tables are in supplementary materials not provided in the PDF: Table S1 (baseline characteristics and genetic polymorphism distributions), Table S2 (clinical outcomes pre/post by group), Table S3 (response rates VA vs. SA), Table S4 (between-group comparisons AG vs. SC, PB, WL), Table S5–S7 (baseline analysis by genotype), Table S8 (acupoint allocation responders vs. non-responders), Table S9 (baseline demographics responders vs. non-responders), Table S10 (pain scale improvements responders vs. non-responders), Table S11 (3279 genes associated with VBM changes), Table S12 (GO enrichment for GABRB3), Table S13 (GO enrichment for PLS+ genes), Table S14 (GO enrichment for PLS− genes), Figure S1 (acupoint locations), Figure S2 (genetic polymorphism distributions), Figure S3 (clinical outcomes), Figure S4 (treatment response rates and between-group comparisons), Figure S5 (logistic regression baseline covariables), Figure S6 (hub gene network visualizations).

The paper states that both SA and VA groups used 'standardized procedures' with needle manipulation for Deqi sensation induction. It is unclear whether the sham acupuncture (non-acupoint needling) was intended to produce true Deqi or was administered without the expectation of Deqi. The same language is used for both groups. This ambiguity affects classification of SA as non-penetrating vs. penetrating sham.

The specific four standard acupoints used in the VA group are not listed in the main text; they are referenced to Figure S1 and reference [56] (Guo et al., 2019, Trials). The acupoint names could not be extracted from the main paper text.

The paper does not report quantitative deqi scores or use a validated deqi scale (e.g., MGQ, MASS, SAS). Only the requirement for Deqi induction is mentioned procedurally. No sensory rating data are reported.
Expectancy, credibility, and perceived treatment allocation were not formally assessed or reported. This is not explicitly acknowledged as a limitation in the paper.
Session duration (time needles retained per session) is not explicitly reported for VA or SA groups.

The neuroimaging analysis focuses on structural MRI (VBM of gray matter volume) collected at baseline. No task-fMRI or resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) is reported in this paper despite the study design including both pre- and post-treatment MRI scans. The modality field was set to 'other' as this is structural MRI (T1-weighted), not functional MRI.

The VBM analysis compared genotype groups (AG/GG vs. AA) within the acupuncture group at baseline. It is not entirely clear whether VBM change scores (pre vs. post) were also analyzed; the text refers to 'baseline gray matter VBM comparisons' suggesting cross-sectional baseline analysis only.
The paper states that the AG group comprised n=54 for VBM analysis but does not explicitly report the breakdown by genotype (number of AA vs. AG/GG carriers) used in the VBM comparison.

Exact p-values or cluster-level statistics are not reported for individual VBM clusters beyond the Z-values in Table 2. The paper states thresholds but does not report exact cluster-level p-values for each cluster.

The PLS1 gene weight values visible in Figure 5b are extracted; however, Figure 5b lists the weights as a partially visible table. Some intermediate genes between the top-5 positive and negative genes are indicated by '...' in the figure. These intermediate values could not be extracted.

The arm_id 'AG' is a post-hoc combined group (VA+SA) created after finding no significant difference between the two original acupuncture arms. This combination affects interpretation: the acupuncture group includes both verum and sham needling. The genetic analyses, VBM, and transcriptomic analyses are all conducted on this combined group.

Table 1 reports n values for GABRB3 rs4906902 recessive model in AG as 33/21 (total 54) and responders as 23/8. However, the text states 31 total responders and 23 non-responders. The responder counts in Table 1 for AG under the recessive model (23 AG/GG responders + 8 AA responders = 31) are consistent with the total of 31 responders. This is internally consistent.

The neuroimaging transcriptomics analysis uses gene expression data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA; 6 healthy adult donors) to spatially correlate with VBM results from KOA patients. This cross-species/cross-population inference is acknowledged as a limitation by the authors.

The paper does not report results for the post-treatment MRI scan (2nd MRI scan mentioned in the flow diagram). It is unclear whether longitudinal VBM change analyses were performed; only baseline genotype-group comparisons are reported in the results.
